title: Habiter: à / en / au / aux
summary: Habiter needs the right place preposition: à + city, en + feminine country, au + masculine country, aux + plural country names.
full_explanation: Habiter needs the right place preposition: à + city, en + feminine country, au + masculine country, aux + plural country names. Learn the place first, then lock the preposition. Cities almost always take à: j’habite à Paris, à Lyon, à Montréal. Feminine country names often take en: en France, en Belgique, en Suisse. Masculine country names often take au: au Canada, au Japon, au Maroc. Plural country names take aux: aux États-Unis, aux Pays-Bas. When you are unsure, ask: is this a city, a feminine country, a masculine country, or a plural name? Say each pair aloud. Do not invent English-style “in Paris” calques with en + city. Keep chunks whole: j’habite à + city. Mix with être and greetings so the pattern does not sit alone. Short daily review beats one long cram session for these prepositions.

examples.english: I live in the United States.

deepDive.whyItMatters: Habiter needs the right place preposition: à + city, en + feminine country, au + masculine country, aux + plural country names. This pattern appears constantly in real conversation and in Phase I checkpoints.

sections.heading: Traps
sections.body: Do not translate word-for-word from English every time. Keep French chunks whole. Check gender and articles when a noun is involved.
